title: Reactions and Energy Changes
seo_title: Chemistry 11: Reactions and Energy Changes Worksheets (BC Curriculum)
short_title: types of reactions, balancing equations and ΔH
standard_text: Matter and energy are conserved in chemical reactions: types of reactions, balancing equations, the activity series, and energy changes (ΔH) in exothermic and endothermic reactions, including calorimetry. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Chemistry 11)
meta_desc: Free Chemistry 11 worksheets (BC Curriculum): types of reactions, balancing equations and ΔH. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Exothermic: ΔH is negative. Endothermic: ΔH is positive.
body_html:
How to think about it

Reaction types include synthesis, decomposition, single and double replacement, combustion and neutralization. The activity series predicts whether a single replacement will happen: a metal replaces any metal below it.

Breaking bonds takes energy and making bonds releases it. If more energy is released than absorbed, the reaction is exothermic (ΔH < 0). Calorimetry measures the heat: q = mcΔT.

Example

Will Zn react with CuSO₄ solution?

Is zinc above copper in the activity series?

Answer: yes

Example

A reaction has ΔH = +50 kJ. Exothermic or endothermic?

Positive ΔH

Answer: endothermic

Common mistakes

  • Getting the sign of ΔH backwards.
  • Thinking breaking bonds releases energy.
  • Changing subscripts to balance.

No. There are too many arrows.

items.q: Using the reactivity series (K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Pb > H > Cu > Ag > Au), which metal is more reactive: sodium or gold?
items.e: Higher in the list = loses electrons more easily.

items.q: Does calcium react with hydrochloric acid? (Reactivity series: K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Pb > H > Cu > Ag > Au)
c: Only if the metal is melted.
No, it is below hydrogen in the reactivity series.
items.e: Metals above hydrogen replace it from acids.

items.q: A piece of copper is placed in magnesium sulfate solution. Will a displacement reaction occur? (Reactivity series: K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Pb > H > Cu > Ag > Au)
c: Yes. Copper is more active than magnesium, so it replaces it.
Yes. Any metal replaces any other metal.
No. Metals never react with solutions.
No. Copper is less active than magnesium, so no reaction occurs.
items.e: A metal replaces only metals below it in the reactivity series.

items.q: Complete the word equation: lead oxide + carbon → ? + carbon dioxide
items.e: Carbon takes the oxygen.

items.q: What is the empirical formula of a compound?
c: the actual number of atoms in a molecule
the simplest whole-number ratio of the atoms of each element
items.e: Glucose C₆H₁₂O₆ has the empirical formula CH₂O.

items.q: What is the mole?
c: the volume of 1 L of gas
the amount of substance containing 6.02 × 10²³ particles
items.e: This number is Avogadro's constant.

items.q: What is the molar volume of a gas at 25 °C and 100 kPa (SLC)?
items.e: At SLC 1 mol of any gas occupies 24.8 L.

items.q: 2HF → H<sub>2</sub> + F<sub>2</sub>. Bond energies (kJ/mol): H–F = 567, H–H = 436, F–F = 158. What is the energy change?
items.e: the energy change = broken − formed = 1134 − 594 = +540 kJ.

items.q: What is the specific heat capacity of water used in calorimetry?
items.e: q = m × c × ΔT.

items.q: 2HBr → H<sub>2</sub> + Br<sub>2</sub>. Bond energies (kJ/mol): H–Br = 366, H–H = 436, Br–Br = 193. How much energy is needed to break the bonds in the reactants?
2HCl → H<sub>2</sub> + Cl<sub>2</sub>. Bond energies (kJ/mol): H–Cl = 431, H–H = 436, Cl–Cl = 242. What is the energy change?
items.e: the energy change = broken − formed = 862 − 678 = +184 kJ.

items.q: N<sub>2</sub> + 3H<sub>2</sub> → 2NH<sub>3</sub>. Bond energies (kJ/mol): N≡N = 945, H–H = 436, N–H = 391. What is the energy change?
items.e: the energy change = broken − formed = 2253 − 2346 = −93 kJ.

items.q: 2HI → H<sub>2</sub> + I<sub>2</sub>. Bond energies (kJ/mol): H–I = 299, H–H = 436, I–I = 151. How much energy is released when the product bonds form?
N<sub>2</sub> + 3H<sub>2</sub> → 2NH<sub>3</sub>. Bond energies (kJ/mol): N≡N = 945, H–H = 436, N–H = 391. How much energy is released when the product bonds form?
What is an exothermic reaction?
c: one that takes in energy, so the energy change is positive
one that releases energy to the surroundings, so the energy change is negative
items.e: Combustion and neutralization are exothermic.

items.q: In an energy profile diagram, what is the activation energy?
c: the energy difference between the reactants and the top of the energy barrier
the energy difference between reactants and products
the energy released by the reaction
items.e: the energy change is reactants to products; Ea is reactants to the peak.

items.q: Why is incomplete combustion of fuels dangerous?
c: it can make carbon monoxide, a toxic gas
items.e: CO binds to hemoglobin.

items.q: What is the products of the complete combustion of a hydrocarbon?
items.e: Incomplete combustion can give CO and soot.

items.q: After a while, the aluminum block and the water in Noah's cup stop changing temperature. What state have they reached?
items.e: Energy spreads out until temperatures are equal.

items.q: Arjun drops a silver block at 90 °C into water at 18 °C. Which way does thermal energy flow?
c: from the silver to the water
from the water to the silver
cold flows from the water into the silver
both ways equally, so nothing changes
items.e: Energy flows from hot to cold.

items.q: Ethan mixes 200 g of water at 7 °C with 200 g of water at 67 °C in an insulated cup. What is the final temperature?
items.e: Heat lost = heat gained: (200 × 7 + 200 × 67) ÷ 400 = 37 °C.

items.q: In Aiden's insulated cup, a hot iron block and cool water reach the same temperature. Which statement is true?
c: The heat lost by the metal equals the heat gained by the water.
items.e: Energy is conserved in a closed system.

items.q: Leah mixes 300 g of water at 17 °C with 300 g of water at 67 °C in an insulated cup. What is the final temperature?
items.e: Heat lost = heat gained: (300 × 17 + 300 × 67) ÷ 600 = 42 °C.

items.q: Burning 0.30 g of propan-1-ol (M<sub>r</sub> 60.0) heats 100 g of water by 12.0 K. Calculate the enthalpy of combustion (c = 4.18 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹).
items.e: q = mcΔT = 5020 J; n = 0.00500 mol; the energy change = −q/n = −1000 kJ mol⁻¹.

items.q: Burning 0.60 g of hexane (M<sub>r</sub> 86.0) heats 150 g of water by 18.0 K. Calculate the enthalpy of combustion (c = 4.18 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹).
items.e: q = mcΔT = 11300 J; n = 0.00698 mol; the energy change = −q/n = −1620 kJ mol⁻¹.

items.q: Chloe mixes 150 g of water at 24 °C with 100 g of water at 64 °C in an insulated cup. What is the final temperature?
items.e: Heat lost = heat gained: (150 × 24 + 100 × 64) ÷ 250 = 40 °C.

items.q: Burning 0.40 g of butan-1-ol (M<sub>r</sub> 74.0) heats 200 g of water by 30.0 K. Calculate the enthalpy of combustion (c = 4.18 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹).
items.e: q = mcΔT = 25100 J; n = 0.00541 mol; the energy change = −q/n = −4640 kJ mol⁻¹.

items.q: 50.0 mL of 2.0 mol/L HCl is mixed with 50.0 mL of 2.0 mol/L NaOH. The temperature rises by 13 K. Calculate the enthalpy of neutralization (c = 4.18 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹).
items.e: q = mcΔT = 100 × 4.18 × 13 = 5520 J; n = 0.100 mol; the energy change = −q/n = −55.2 kJ mol⁻¹.

items.e: q = mcΔT = 50.0 × 4.18 × 6.8 = 1420 J; n = 0.0250 mol; the energy change = −q/n = −56.8 kJ mol⁻¹.

items.q: A silver block at 80 °C is placed in water at 18 °C in a closed, insulated cup. Which final temperature is possible?
items.e: The final temperature is between the two starting temperatures.

items.q: In Ethan's insulated cup, a hot aluminum block and cool water reach the same temperature. Which statement is true?
c: The heat lost by the metal equals the heat gained by the water.
items.e: Energy is conserved in a closed system.

items.q: A copper block at 80 °C is placed in water at 20 °C in a closed, insulated cup. Which final temperature is possible?
items.e: The final temperature is between the two starting temperatures.

items.q: Burning 0.60 g of hexane (M<sub>r</sub> 86.0) heats 150 g of water by 12.0 K. Calculate the enthalpy of combustion (c = 4.18 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹).
items.e: q = mcΔT = 7520 J; n = 0.00698 mol; the energy change = −q/n = −1080 kJ mol⁻¹.

items.q: Burning 0.50 g of ethanol (M<sub>r</sub> 46.0) heats 200 g of water by 12.0 K. Calculate the enthalpy of combustion (c = 4.18 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹).
items.e: q = mcΔT = 10000 J; n = 0.0109 mol; the energy change = −q/n = −923 kJ mol⁻¹.

items.q: Sofia drops an aluminum block at 90 °C into water at 22 °C. Which way does thermal energy flow?
c: from the aluminum to the water
from the water to the aluminum
cold flows from the water into the aluminum
both ways equally, so nothing changes
items.e: Energy flows from hot to cold.

items.e: The final temperature is between the two starting temperatures.
